claims.statement: The 2024-03 HO-3 Section II Coverage E pays damages for which an insured is legally liable because of bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense for covered claims or suits; Coverage E applies to insured locations and personal activities, applies separately to each insured, and does not increase the applicable limit through that separation.

HO-3 Section II Coverage F provides no-fault medical-payments coverage for necessary medical expenses from accidental bodily injury, including specified injuries away from an insured location, while its business exclusion preserves only activities ordinarily incidental to nonbusiness pursuits and its animal-away-from-location grant excludes animals used in connection with a business.

The HO-3 baseline Section II exclusions remove bodily injury and property damage arising from a business or business pursuit and separately constrain business-use vehicles, watercraft, and animals, subject to the stated incidental-to-nonbusiness exception.

HO 04 42 provides attached-endorsement coverage for an insured's bodily injury, property damage, or personal injury liability arising from an occurrence connected with a lawful incidental occupancy at premises used with the residence, where the occupancy is subordinate to residential use and does not materially change the premises' residential character; it provides a defense until the applicable limit is paid or coverage does not apply.

HO 04 42 uses the policy's insured status rather than expanding who is insured, and it excludes incidental occupancy away from the residence and numerous professional, care, product, employment, vehicle, equipment, pollution, disease, intentional-act, and criminal-act exposures; it also excludes unpermitted or non-residentially subordinate business activity.

HO 04 42 refers its liability grant to the applicable limit but does not state a separate dollar liability amount in the cited grant, while its later limit provisions are written for covered property; its claim duties include prompt notice, forwarding legal papers, cooperation, inspection, evidence preservation, and consent before voluntary payment or settlement.

HO 24 71 modifies the policy to provide personal-liability coverage for bodily injury or property damage and medical-payments coverage arising from an insured's business pursuit, defined as a continuous, regular, or profit-motivated business activity conducted from the residence or elsewhere; it covers specified premises, insured acts, and legally responsible persons without making another person an insured.

HO 24 71 sets a $100,000 maximum for the sum of all liability damages arising out of business pursuits, shared across insureds, claimants, claims, suits, and occurrences; payments reduce the amount available, defense costs do not reduce it, and the defense duty ends when payment exhausts the limit, while the endorsement does not increase the policy's personal-liability or medical-payments limits.

HO 24 73 modifies the policy for covered farming and farm premises, includes resident related household members and persons or organizations acting within the scope of duties performed for the insured in connection with covered farming, and grants bodily-injury/property-damage personal liability plus medical-payments coverage arising from covered personal activities, farming, or farm premises.

HO 24 73 applies the applicable personal-liability and medical-payments limits without stating a separate farm dollar limit in its cited grant, shares the limit across insureds and claimants, ends the defense after exhaustion, and retains business, professional-services, employee, workers-compensation, and business-animal exclusions.

HO 24 73 imposes farming-specific duties to maintain structures and animal controls, use care with agricultural materials and machinery, preserve operational records, report farm-operation claims, and notify the insurer of material changes, expansion, discontinuance, or transfer of control of the farming operation.

HO 24 82 modifies the policy by providing separate Personal Injury Coverage for an insured who is legally responsible for damages arising from covered offenses during the policy period, including false arrest, detention or imprisonment, malicious prosecution, wrongful eviction or entry, invasion of private occupancy, defamation, and privacy violations; the offense must arise from covered residence use or personal activities.

HO 24 82 excludes personal injury arising from business pursuits and business activities conducted from an insured location, except for activities ordinarily incidental to nonbusiness pursuits; its Personal Injury Limit of Liability is shared for all damages from an occurrence, is reduced by payments, does not increase through multiple insureds or claims, and ends the defense after judgments or settlements exhaust it.

HO 04 96 is titled as a no-Section-II liability-coverages endorsement, but its supplied operative text expressly grants personal liability, medical-payments, and defense coverage and supplies a general limit section without an operative Section II deletion clause; the source therefore requires reconciliation of the attached form, declarations, and controlling policy text before determining Section II availability.

Texas underwriting controls separately direct referral or non-acceptance for material business operations, agricultural activity, livestock, and certain animal exposures, and for premises used for business operations, professional services, production, farming, animal keeping, crop activity, or agricultural equipment; these are internal appetite controls rather than contractual coverage grants or exclusions.

The HO-4 2021-10 Coverage E pays damages for bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense by counsel of the insurer's choice; its business exclusion applies to business conducted from any location, its defense expenses and taxed costs are in addition to damages, and its own premises, vehicle, watercraft, property, and damages exclusions control the result.

The HO-6 2023-02 Coverage E pays damages for bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense against a covered suit; its business exclusion allows a result only when coverage is expressly provided by the policy, and its additional liability-related coverages remain separate and subject to their own exclusions, conditions, and duties.

The HO-3 2024-03, HO-4 2021-10, and HO-6 2023-02 base Coverage E grants quoted here address bodily injury and property damage rather than supplying the separate offense-based personal-injury grant provided by an attached HO 24 82 endorsement; a personal-injury allegation therefore requires review of the applicable attached endorsement and its exclusions.

The base editions use the applicable liability limit rather than creating a new numeric limit in the Coverage E grant, apply coverage separately to insureds without increasing the occurrence limit, and end the defense duty on exhaustion; HO-4 additionally places defense expenses and taxed costs in addition to damages, while HO-3 and HO-6 state their own requested-expense provisions.

The liability claim-handling guidance is an internal workflow rather than contract language: after notice it directs file opening, party and policy identification, demand and service preservation, policy and endorsement review, investigation, defense coordination, authority-controlled resolution, recovery protection, and documented closure without amending the applicable policy.

The claims manual's liability chapter directs handlers to separate facts from allegations, preserve evidence, evaluate liability before stating a position, inspect property when useful, and refer serious, complex, intentional, criminal, governmental, professional-service, environmental, structural, product, or completed-work allegations; its 30-day notice screen is an internal handling control and does not replace the applicable policy's prompt-notice condition.
